result.summary: This residential street features continuous sidewalks on both sides, providing a dedicated space for pedestrians. However, the environment lacks safety features such as marked crosswalks or traffic calming, and parked cars create significant visual obstructions for anyone attempting to cross the roadway.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction
hazards.description: Parked cars along both curbs block sightlines between drivers and pedestrians, especially at potential crossing points.
hazards.location_in_image: Along both sides of the roadway

hazards.name: Lack of Crossing Infrastructure
hazards.description: The absence of marked crosswalks or signage on this long residential block may lead to unpredictable crossing behavior.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions (bulb-outs) to improve visibility between pedestrians and drivers and shorten the crossing distance.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Add marked crosswalks with high-visibility paint to provide designated and visible crossing points for pedestrians.

interventions.title: Speed Humps
interventions.description: Implement speed humps or other traffic calming measures to naturally slow vehicle speeds in this residential setting.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment features a wide concrete walkway directly adjacent to an unmarked two-lane road, lacking any physical buffer or street trees. The frontage is a mix of residential row houses and a commercial building with a blank wall, and the pavement shows signs of wear and cracking.

hazards.name: Lack of pedestrian-vehicle separation
hazards.description: There is no physical buffer, such as trees or a furniture zone, between the wide sidewalk and the travel lane.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the curb line in the foreground

hazards.name: Uneven pavement
hazards.description: The concrete walkway shows significant cracking and uneven surfaces which could be a trip hazard.
hazards.location_in_image: Across the paved area in front of the buildings

interventions.title: Street Trees and Planting Strips
interventions.description: Install a planting buffer with street trees to provide physical and psychological separation from traffic.

interventions.title: Pavement Repair
interventions.description: Resurface the cracked concrete walkway to ensure a smooth, accessible path for all users.

interventions.title: Roadway Markings
interventions.description: Add center lines and edge lines to the roadway to better define travel lanes and encourage slower speeds.

result.summary: The image shows a signalized intersection in a mixed-use area with marked zebra crosswalks and basic sidewalk infrastructure. While pedestrian crossings are designated, the lack of physical buffers and long crossing distances across multiple lanes present safety challenges.

hazards.name: Long Crossing Distance
hazards.description: Pedestrians must cross multiple lanes of traffic without a median refuge island.

hazards.name: Lack of Sidewalk Buffer
hazards.description: The sidewalk is directly adjacent to the travel lane with no planting strip or parked car buffer in the immediate foreground.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs at the corners to reduce crossing distance and improve pedestrian visibility.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Add a raised island in the center of the wide crossing to allow pedestrians to cross in stages.

interventions.title: Leading Pedestrian Interval
interventions.description: Program traffic signals to give pedestrians a head start before vehicles get a green light.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment is characterized by a narrow, poorly maintained sidewalk directly adjacent to a two-lane roadway. Significant obstructions like utility poles and fences further restrict the walking path, and there is a complete lack of separation or safety features for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Narrow and Obstructed Walkway
hazards.description: The sidewalk is extremely narrow and further constricted by a utility pole and adjacent fencing, forcing pedestrians into a very tight space or into the roadway.
hazards.location_in_image: Left foreground and center along the sidewalk edge

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Buffer
hazards.description: There is no physical separation or buffer zone between the narrow sidewalk and the travel lane, increasing the risk of vehicle-pedestrian conflict.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the entire length of the visible sidewalk

hazards.name: Poor Pavement Condition
hazards.description: The sidewalk surface is cracked, uneven, and degraded, creating significant trip hazards.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Widening and Repair
interventions.description: Expand the sidewalk to meet ADA standards and resurface it to provide a smooth, continuous walking path.

interventions.title: Utility Pole Relocation
interventions.description: Move utility poles out of the pedestrian clear zone to a furniture zone or behind the sidewalk to remove physical barriers.

interventions.title: Street Buffer/Planting Strip
interventions.description: Introduce a planting strip or furniture zone between the sidewalk and the curb to provide physical and psychological separation from traffic.
